title: The Lion, the Bull and the Jackal
text:
Pingalaka, the lion king of a forest, once heard a tremendous bellow and was secretly terrified. The sound came from Sanjivaka, a bull who had been abandoned by a merchant and was now grazing by the river. Damanaka, an ambitious jackal who had lost favor at court, saw an opening. He went to the bull, brought him before the king, and arranged a friendship between them.

The friendship worked too well. Lion and bull became inseparable. Sanjivaka taught the king calm and wisdom, and Pingalaka spent his days in conversation and stopped hunting, so his courtiers, the jackals among them, went hungry and lost influence.

Damanaka decided to undo what he had built. He went to the lion and whispered that the bull was plotting to seize the throne. Then he went to the bull and whispered that the lion planned to kill and eat him. Each was told to watch for signs in the other's manner. When they next met, each saw what he had been told to expect. They fought, and the lion killed his friend. Only afterward did Pingalaka grieve for what he had done, and the jackal took the post of chief minister.
lesson: When someone brings you private warnings about a trusted colleague, ask what the messenger stands to gain. Talk directly to the person accused before you act on a story you heard secondhand.
people: Pingalaka the lion, Sanjivaka the bull, Damanaka and Karataka the jackals
